system.biography:
Background

Fifth-generation @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, a native of Antioch (modern Turkey), Embraced by a post-Thera-dispersal veteran while traveling with Alexander the Great's army. Settled permanently in Antioch, protecting and improving the city through every subsequent political upheaval (the Crusades, the Ottoman conquest, Turkish nationalism) by focusing solely on Antioch's interests. His lineage has included over a hundred members at its peak; roughly forty remain after crusade losses and Sunni nationalist hunting. He oversees merchant and shipping interests in Antioch's tradition, with lineage members now running Chicago brokerages and Shanghai commodity exchanges.

He survived early @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} purges of Methuselahs through prudence, bribery, and occasional strategic redirection of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} war parties at rivals, withdrawing into shadow via arts unknown to neonates when necessary. He serves on Courts of Blood once or twice a century for both Sabbat and antitribu, always adjudicating within the participants' own accepted code rather than his own views, and quietly mentors promising neonates toward independence from the Sabbat without telling other vampires how to run their affairs.

Roleplaying Hints

Zarathustra is patient beyond mortal comprehension, speaks in measured diplomatic tones, and never reveals more of his true power than a situation requires. He judges by each party's own code rather than imposing his own.

Disciplines (as printed, converted to owned Discipline Items at Storyteller discretion): Dominate, Obtenebration, Potence, plus additional Methuselah-tier mastery per Storyteller discretion (Auspex and Obfuscate suggested for his shadow-craft and information-gathering).
system.notes: Sect: technically outside both @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} structures; serves as an independent arbiter respected by both. Convert Disciplines to owned power Items at very high (Elder/Methuselah) ratings.

system.description: By meeting your subject's gaze and winning a Mental Challenge, you implant a more complex command, optionally tied to a specific trigger event, to be carried out immediately or later.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By winning a Mental Challenge while holding your victim's gaze, you can erase, alter, or implant up to fifteen minutes of memory per challenge, or question the subject to recall details they otherwise might not share.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Rather than requiring eye contact, you may use Dominate through skin-to-skin contact alone (a Physical Challenge may be needed on unwilling subjects). The touch need not be maintained while issuing the command, but only one command may be given per contact; using Dominate again requires touching the subject anew.

A combination power blending Obtenebration and Obfuscate. The Magister summons fluttering shadows that behave like moths drawn to flame, flocking to the nearest light sources — torches, candles, oil lamps — and dousing them. An entire area can be plunged into darkness almost instantly, leaving anyone unprepared for the dark completely helpless. Each success produces one shadow, which douses any flame up to the size of a torch before vanishing; larger fires require multiple shadows to extinguish. Shadows in excess of the available flames flap about causing confusion and fear before dissipating into whatever dark place spawned them. They cause no direct damage, though they may collide with people in their flight.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis I: Masters of the State, Book One: Magisters
system.duration: Until all nearby light sources are doused

system.description: A combination power blending Obtenebration and Potence. Where Arms of Ahriman lets a Lasombra summon tentacles of pure shadow to grip and strike, this bastardized variant grants those pseudopods far greater strength and endurance, catching Cainites used to the ordinary manifestation off guard. Each success summons one tentacle, emerging from any nearby patch of shadow (beneath furniture, from within the vampire's own cloak, and so on). Every tentacle is eight feet long and has Strength and Dexterity equal to twice the wielder's Obtenebration rating. The vampire may feed a tentacle additional Blood Points, one for one, raising its ratings further. A Dark Steel tentacle deals Strength+2 crushing damage, has six health levels of its own, and — like the wielder — takes extra harm from fire and sunlight.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis I: Masters of the State, Book One: Magisters
system.bloodCost: 2 Blood Points, plus 1 per point of tentacle enhancement

system.description: While standing in a naturally occurring shadow, spend two Blood Traits and win a Static Mental Challenge against a seven-Trait difficulty to shift your position up to 50 steps to another natural shadow within line of sight, carrying your clothes and possessions. Bringing along an unwilling companion or using the power to escape restraint requires an additional Willpower Trait and winning a Physical Challenge.
system.bloodCost: 2 Blood Traits (+1 Willpower for a companion)

system.description: You may make a single retest on any challenge of sheer physical strength, even against an opponent relying on stamina or speed to resist, at no cost.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: You may use the Bomb symbol in challenges of strength, which defeats Rock and Paper, ties with other Bombs, and loses only to Scissors, requiring no expenditure.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description:
Facetiously named, this power allows the Kindred to physically knock another character away from herself with the slightest of touches. Although this power does no damage in and of itself, its use is quite humbling — to be hurled away from an elder in a social setting has its embarrassing repercussions. Some Kindred use this power surreptitiously, touching their victims and sending them reeling across the room; others use it as a not-so-subtle display of their might, giving their victim a casual slap with overwhelming results.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait and must succeed in a physical challenge to touch the target (this may be done surreptitiously, but the player may not make use of other Potence benefits). The challenge is not required if the subject allows the player to touch him (a handshake, a “friendly” hand on the shoulder, etc). This power hurls the victim 20 feet directly away from the invoking character. If the subject strikes a wall or other solid obstacle, he suffers two health levels of bashing damage. Otherwise, the character needs to win a static physical challenge against six Traits to remain standing.

You may double the range of your sight and hearing and sharpen your other senses to remarkable acuity, perceiving things ordinary folk cannot. A sudden sensory assault, such as a loud noise or strong odor, numbs the affected sense for the rest of the scene and stuns you for a turn unless you spend a Willpower Trait. You may also receive uncontrollable visions of past or future events.

Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

Originally used to lead warrior-caste mystics on vision quests, this vizier technique lets a willing seer bring companions with him into the astral realms. All would-be participants must form an unbroken chain of physical contact with the character. Spend a Blood Trait for each "follower" you wish to bring along, up to a maximum of half your permanent Mental Traits (rounded down), then leave your body as per Psychic Projection. Each follower is treated as though she knows Psychic Projection regardless of her actual Auspex rating, using the leader's rolled successes. On the astral plane, followers must remain within roughly 100 feet of the leader, tethered to him and unable to break the connection. Any follower who loses physical contact with the leader instantly returns to her body and loses three Mental Traits, falling unconscious for the rest of the night if this reduces her to zero Mental Traits.
system.bloodCost: 1 Blood Trait per follower (max half permanent Mental Traits, rounded down)

system.description: Once hidden from sight, you may move about at a walk and remain unnoticed, automatically becoming visible only if you speak, make loud noise, or interact with your surroundings.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: Your features appear bland and unremarkable to onlookers, or by spending a Mental Trait you can assume a specific guise, copying another's appearance up to the Social Traits you can afford to match, lasting until you sleep, are knocked out, or die.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description:
Reaches into a target's self-image and lets the Malkavian assume the appearance and false memories of whoever has most shaped (or damaged) that self-image — a sire, a parent, a priest, or whoever the target's own psyche supplies.

MET System: Win a Social Challenge against the victim. On a win, you gain a free retest on your very next use of Dementation, Dominate, or Presence against that same victim. Once the retest is used, the power's knowledge fades unless you spend a Willpower Trait to keep it active for one further retest (this is expensive, but more certain than triggering the power again from scratch). You may only claim one retest per challenge this way. This power relies heavily on the target's own good-faith roleplaying — if the subject's player won't cooperate, don't force it with a Storyteller ruling.
